subject.title: refactor: move MCP OAuth state to SQLite

question: Should OpenClaw ship the immediate Doctor-only MCP OAuth cutover, where existing JSON credentials are unusable at runtime until migrated and logout tombstones prevent later resurrection?
rationale: The implementation and proof can establish mechanics, but only the security owner can accept the credential-storage boundary and deliberate upgrade behavior for existing installations.

options.title: Approve guarded cutover
options.body: Accept shared SQLite as the sole runtime owner, require Doctor for legacy import, and ship the documented operator migration step.

options.title: Require more upgrade hardening
options.body: Hold merge until the security owner identifies an additional startup, recovery, or migration safeguard that does not reintroduce runtime JSON fallback.

options.title: Defer the migration
options.body: Pause this PR and retain the current JSON store until the credential cutover and operator experience receive a different approved design.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded cutover
recommendation.body: Accept shared SQLite as the sole runtime owner, require Doctor for legacy import, and ship the documented operator migration step.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle was explicitly requested to accept or reject the migration and security contract.
